# Kioku View output rules

Submit a gzip-compressed tar archive with these files at its root:

- `index.html` (required): a nonempty UTF-8 HTML document. A minimal document is
  `<!doctype html><html lang="ja"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>View</title></head><body><h1>View</h1></body></html>`.
- `summary.md` (optional): UTF-8 Markdown with the key findings and Wiki paths
  as citations.
- `data.json` (optional): a single valid UTF-8 JSON value. Prefer a JSON object
  with meaningful keys for machine readers.
- `assets/` (optional): CSS, PNG, and JPEG files. Names use ASCII letters,
  digits, underscores, hyphens and dots. Start each component with a letter,
  digit or underscore. Use relative paths. Exclude links, duplicates and extra files.

Use semantic HTML and native `details`/`summary` for disclosure. JavaScript,
SVG, forms, iframes and event attributes are prohibited. Use unique attribute names on each element. For metadata use UTF-8 charset, viewport or description.
An `a[href]` can target a local fragment (`#status`) or cite a Wiki page
(`wiki/index.md`). Kioku shows Wiki citations alongside the View. Write external
source addresses as text, or cite their Wiki pages.
Use `img[src]` for bundled PNG/JPEG, and `link[rel="stylesheet"]` for bundled CSS.
A CSS `url(...)` can refer to a bundled image relative to the stylesheet
(or to the document for inline CSS). External URLs and data URLs are prohibited.
Inline `style` attributes accept declarations. Stylesheets and `<style>` support
local layout and animation. Use `@media (max-width: 600px) { .grid { display: block } }`
for responsive layout. CSS may not contain the characters `<`, backslash, or NUL.
Use the listed at-rules and functions below.

Keep the saved prompt focused on what to show, the sources to use and how to
organize the result. A few short paragraphs or bullets are a useful starting
point. Specify any required optional files and keep generated content concise.

Allowed HTML elements: a, abbr, address, article, aside, b, bdi, bdo, blockquote, body, br, caption, cite, code, col, colgroup, data, dd, del, details, dfn, div, dl, dt, em, figcaption, figure, footer, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, head, header, hgroup, hr, html, i, img, ins, kbd, li, link, main, mark, meta, meter, nav, ol, p, pre, progress, q, rp, rt, ruby, s, samp, section, small, span, strong, style, sub, summary, sup, table, tbody, td, tfoot, th, thead, time, title, tr, u, ul, var, wbr.
Global attributes: class, dir, hidden, id, lang, role, style, tabindex, title, plus aria-, data- prefixes.
Additional attributes by element:
- a: href
- col: span
- colgroup: span
- data: value
- details: name, open
- img: alt, height, loading, src, width
- li: value
- link: href, media, rel
- meta: charset, content, name
- meter: high, low, max, min, optimum, value
- ol: reversed, start, type
- progress: max, value
- style: media
- td: colspan, headers, rowspan
- th: abbr, colspan, headers, rowspan, scope
- time: datetime

CSS at-rules (stylesheets and style elements): @-webkit-keyframes, @container, @keyframes, @layer, @media, @starting-style, @supports.
CSS functions: abs, attr, blur, brightness, calc, circle, clamp, color, color-mix, conic-gradient, contrast, counter, counters, cubic-bezier, dir, drop-shadow, ellipse, env, fit-content, grayscale, has, hsl, hsla, hue-rotate, hwb, inset, invert, is, lab, lang, lch, light-dark, linear, linear-gradient, matrix, matrix3d, max, min, minmax, mod, not, nth-child, nth-last-child, nth-last-of-type, nth-of-type, oklab, oklch, opacity, path, perspective, polygon, radial-gradient, rem, repeat, repeating-conic-gradient, repeating-linear-gradient, repeating-radial-gradient, rgb, rgba, rotate, rotate3d, rotatex, rotatey, rotatez, round, saturate, scale, scale3d, scalex, scaley, scalez, selector, sepia, sign, skew, skewx, skewy, steps, translate, translate3d, translatex, translatey, translatez, var, where, and url() for bundled images.

Limits: 16 MiB compressed, 8 MiB expanded, 128 archive entries (files and directories), 180 bytes per archive path, 1 MiB per text file, 256 KiB per CSS source, 12 MiB rendered document, HTML depth 96, 16 megapixels per image and 24 megapixels total (1 megapixel = 1,048,576 pixels).
